newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain govt says won't enter labour reform fray yet.
newsitem.headline: Spain govt says won't enter labour reform fray yet.

text.p: Spanish Labour Minister Javier Arenas on Wednesday reaffirmed the need for a reform of the labour market, but said the government would not intervene as yet in negotiations between unions and employers.

"Spanish society needs new formulas which establish labour stability rather than precariousness in employment, which bring security rather than the current uncertainty and which stop excluding young people from more solid labour relations," Arenas said at an economic conference in Madrid.
However government proposals are on hold for the moment.
"We have answers but we won't present them until the social dialogue is over," he said.
"As yet (the government) has no proposal on the table. We will not be more specific until the dialogue between unions and employers develops."
The government would only intervene if unions and employers fail to reach an agreement, he said.
"We want this to have a happy ending. But if an agreement is not reached, the government will make its proposals and will start talks with unions and employers," he said.
Arenas said the government was not putting a time limit on the process, but the situation was urgent.
He estimated that the process should last until the first months of 1997, adding that he hoped an agreement would be reached without the government having to intervene.
